newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU Commission hopes restore Irish peace fund cut.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission hopes restore Irish peace fund cut.

text.p: The European Commissioner for regional policy said on Friday she hoped the European Parliament would review the decision of its budgetary committee to cut special funding for the Northern Ireland peace process.
"I still hope that parliament will review the decision...of the budget committee," Monika Wulf-Mathies told a news conference in Dublin.
The European parliament's budgetary committee recently voted to reduce funding for 1997 for the EU's peace initiative for Northern Ireland and the six border counties of Ireland.
It proposed a cut of 78 million punts ($125 million) in the special EU peace and reconciliation fund.
This would reduce the 1997 allocation to 47 million punts from 125 million, putting at risk dozens of schemes and cross-border projects involving voluntary bodies such as women's groups and farmers.
"It is the wrong political message. People in Northern Ireland are scared that what they have started to establish might be ended by having no funds," Wulf-Mathies said.
"For the sake of the political signal in a very difficult and crucial moment of the peace process but for very practical reasons...I hope the decision can be revised," she added.

Under the EU's budget procedure, the matter goes to a full vote of parliament on October 24 and then to conciliation between the parliament and the Council of Ministers, which shares budgetary authority under the co-decision process.
Wulf-Mathies was in Dublin to address a meeting of the EU's Committee of the Regions and for meetings with the Irish ministers for finance, tourism and trade, and tranport, energy and communications.
